problems.device: planar solid oxide fuel cell single cell with nickel-yttria-stabilized-zirconia anode support
problems.failure: Redox cycling of the Ni-YSZ anode during start/stop events causes irreversible anode volume change: re-oxidation expands the nickel phase, rearranges the anode microstructure (nickel agglomeration and coarsening), and builds tensile stress at the anode-electrolyte interface until the cell cracks or the electrode delaminates, so the stack loses sealing integrity and power density after repeated starts.

problems.failure: Thermal cycling between 25 C and 800 C during start/stop drives differential expansion between the electrolyte, the anode, and the glass-ceramic seal; repeated cycles open microcracks in the seal and at the cathode-electrolyte interface, raising gas crossover and ohmic loss until the stack fails to reach operating voltage.
problems.constraint: survive 500 thermal cycles from 25 C to 800 C at 5 C/min heating rate while holding open-circuit voltage above 1.0 V and keeping seal leakage below 1 percent of fuel flow, without increasing stack mass above 2 percent

seal leakage below 1 percent of fuel flow
stack mass increase below 2 percent

at least 3 percent compressor energy reduction vs the fixed monthly cadence
